11 A rod is pivoted at point O.
A force F is applied to the rod at point W, as shown.
F
X
W
rod
O
Y
What is the moment of the force F about O?
A
F  distance OX
B
F  distance OY
C
F  distance WO
D
F  distance WX

hints: Notice $F$ is applied at W at an angle to the rod, and there are dashed lines with right-angle marks at X and at Y.
Recall the moment about O is $F$ multiplied by the perpendicular distance from O to the line of action of $F$, not just the distance along the rod.
Compare OX, OY, WO and WX and check which one starts at O and meets the extended line of $F$ at 90 degrees.
walkthrough: Identify the pivot as O and the point of application as W, with force $F$ tilted to the rod.
State the rule: moment about a point $=$ force $\times$ perpendicular distance from the point to the line of action of the force.
Extend the line of action of $F$ through W and look for the line from O that meets it at 90 degrees.
The diagram shows this as the dashed segment OY, with a right-angle mark at Y, while WO and OX lie along the rod and WX does not start at O.
Therefore the moment arm is distance OY and the moment is $F \times$ distance OY. This is option B.

A.explanation: Distance OX lies along the rod and is not the perpendicular distance from O to the line of action of $F$.

B.explanation: Distance OY is drawn from pivot O perpendicular to the line of action of $F$, so $F \times OY$ is the moment about O.

C.explanation: Distance WO is along the rod from O to the point of application W, but $F$ is not at 90 degrees to the rod so WO is not perpendicular to $F$.

D.explanation: Distance WX is part of the rod beyond W and does not measure the perpendicular distance from O to the line of $F$.
